service.description: We offer live music for nonprofit galas, association award nights, chamber annual dinners and company award ceremonies in Denver and across Colorado, with reception acts, dinner ensembles and dance bands that work around remarks, auctions, videos and walk-ups.

props.title: Gala entertainment in Denver
props.lede: You've planned every part of the program, and the last thing you want is music playing over your emcee. We'll plan the music around your program with you. That can mean a reception act as the doors open, dinner music your guests can easily talk over, quiet for the emcee, and a dance floor after the last award.

headingText.html: We work with nonprofit galas and fundraisers, association award nights, chamber annual dinners and company award ceremonies.

props.title: Watch our jazz duo play.
props.lede: Our jazz duo plays guitar and upright bass, and it’s a lovely choice for a gala reception or dinner. Once the awards are done, we can bring in a different act for the dancing.

props.title: Live music for every part of your gala program
props.lede: We'll go over the flow of the evening with whoever is running your program, and the bandleader will follow your emcee throughout the event.

rows.text: We can have a reception act playing when your first guests walk in, at a volume the check-in table can easily talk over.
The band can stop before your speaker reaches the podium, and we'll have a microphone ready for them.
The band can play at the level of the conversation for the whole meal. A trio usually does this better than a full band turned down.
If you're showing a video, the band will stop, we'll plan the switch to the house audio ahead of time, and the band can come back in after the applause.

rows.term: The auction and the paddle raise
rows.text: The band will stay quiet during the bidding unless your auctioneer would like some music, and we can play a short piece as each lot closes.
We can play music for each honoree from the moment their name is read until they reach the podium, then stop as soon as they get there. We'll just need the names and the order ahead of time.
A dance band or DJ can take over without a long break to change things over.

props.title: Gala bands, DJs & musicians
props.lede: You can have the same musicians all night or three different acts. Either way, it can all go on one contract with one sound system.

rows.text: Great choices include the jazz duo, a solo pianist, a Spanish guitarist, or a string quartet for a black-tie event. If you'd like something more modern, check out Last Consulate, with upright bass over slow, laid-back electronic music.
We'd suggest the jazz trio, with the drummer playing brushes to keep it soft, or the Americana trio for a gala at a ranch, a barn or up in the mountains.

The soul and R&B band is great on a ballroom floor, the yacht rock band is perfect for a crowd that loves to sing, and live band karaoke lets your guests take the mic. You could also book the DJ on their own or with a live musician playing along.

props.html: Looking for more ideas, music and otherwise? Check out our gala entertainment ideas. Planning a party after the program? Learn more about after-party entertainment.

Planning a company award night? Take a look at our corporate entertainment to learn more about vendor setup and purchase orders. We also play client dinners. If it’s the last night of a mountain retreat, learn more about our corporate retreats.
Looking for stage sizes and power details? Check out our technical page. You can read more booking answers in our planner questions.

items.q: Do you play during the live auction and the paddle raise?
items.a: In our experience, most auctioneers prefer quiet during the bidding. The band will usually start again when the auctioneer hands the microphone back.

items.q: How loud can the band get?
items.a: Once the dancing starts, the band can turn it up as far as the venue allows. Let us know the venue's sound limit and curfew when you book and we'll plan the night around them.

items.q: What do you need from the venue?
items.a: If it’s a hotel, we'll need to know when we can use the loading dock and the elevators. We'll also need one or two dedicated 20-amp circuits, depending on the size of the act. We'd love to see the flow of the evening, too, including when your program needs the music to stop. We can send whatever paperwork your venue or your finance team needs.

items.q: Do you work with our emcee and auctioneer?
items.a: Yes. We'll have a microphone for your emcee and one for your auctioneer, and we'll go over the plan with both of them ahead of time. If your emcee is a board member doing it for the first time, we're glad to walk through it with them before the doors open.

items.q: How far ahead should we book entertainment for a gala?
items.a: Whenever you're ready. Many committees pick the venue and the honorees first and come to the entertainment later, and we're happy to hear from you at any point. Tell us the date and the venue, and we'll come back with a recommendation and a price.

props.title: Send us the flow of the evening and we'll plan the music with you.
props.lede: From a solo musician to a full band, we'd love to help with your gala. We'll size the sound to the venue, and you'll have a personal point of contact for the event.
